messages.content: I'm planning a series of long weekend getaways for the upcoming year and I need to know when they'll occur in my country. Could you fetch me the list of long weekends for Canada in the year 2023? I'd like to integrate this information into my holiday planning app.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑look calendar of the **long weekends** that Canadians will experience in 2023.  
(“Long weekend” means a holiday that falls on a weekday adjacent to a weekend, giving you at least three consecutive days off.)

| Date(s) | Holiday | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| **Dec 31 2022 – Jan 2 2023** | New Year’s Day (observed) | New Year’s Day fell on Sunday Jan 1, so the holiday was observed on Monday Jan 2. |
| **Feb 18–20 2023** | Family Day (Ontario, BC, Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba) | All of these provinces observe Family Day on the third Monday of February. |
| **Apr 7–9 2023** | Good Friday (most provinces) | Good Friday is a statutory holiday in Ontario, BC, Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, and several others. |
| **May 20–22 2023** | Victoria Day (all provinces) | Victoria Day is celebrated on the last Monday before May 25. |
| **Jul 1–3 2023** | Canada Day (all provinces) | Canada Day is on Friday Jul 1, giving a long weekend. |
| **Sep 2–4 2023** | Labour Day (all provinces) | Labour Day is always on the first Monday in September. |
| **Oct 7–9 2023** | Thanksgiving (all provinces) | Thanksgiving is on the second Monday in October. |
| **Dec 23–25 2023** | Christmas Day (all provinces) | Christmas Day is on Monday Dec 25, creating a long weekend. |

### Things to keep in mind

* **Provincial variations** – Some holidays (e.g., Family Day, Good Friday) are not observed in every province. If you’re planning trips in a specific province, double‑check the local holiday schedule.
* **Observed vs. actual dates** – When a holiday falls on a weekend, many provinces move the holiday to the following Monday (or sometimes the preceding Friday). Those “observed” dates are what create the long weekends listed above.
* **Other regional holidays** – Certain territories and provinces have additional holidays that can create long weekends (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador, St. George’s Day in Prince Edward Island). These are not included in the table because they’re not nationwide.

For the most accurate and up‑to‑date holiday information, you can consult the Government of Canada’s official holiday calendar or your provincial government’s public holiday page. Happy planning!
